# Polarization-Selective Phenomena in Whispering Gallery Mode Resonators

Researchers have experimentally demonstrated controlled polarization-selective phenomena in a whispering gallery mode (WGM) resonator, marking a significant advance in the manipulation of light polarization states within compact optical systems. Whispering gallery mode resonators, known for their high quality factors and ability to confine light through total internal reflection along curved boundaries, offer a versatile platform for exploring polarization-dependent optical effects.

In this study, the researchers observed efficient polarization conversion of light—reaching approximately 75%—in a silica microsphere resonator coupled to a tapered optical fiber. This coupling configuration is widely used in WGM resonator experiments due to its ability to efficiently launch light into the resonator's whispering gallery modes while maintaining precise control over the input and output coupling conditions. The high conversion efficiency observed represents a substantial polarization transformation, highlighting the potential of this platform for applications in polarization control and manipulation.

Achieving this level of conversion efficiency proved to be critically dependent on the proper optimization of the polarization state of the light propagating through the tapered fiber prior to coupling into the microsphere. This sensitivity underscores the importance of precise polarization alignment in the input light to maximize the interaction between orthogonally polarized whispering gallery modes within the resonator, suggesting that the underlying conversion mechanism relies on specific phase-matching or coupling conditions that are strongly polarization-dependent.

To provide theoretical insight into the observed phenomena, the researchers developed a simplified analytical model that treats the microsphere resonator as an equivalent ring resonator. This approach reduces the complexity of the three-dimensional whispering gallery mode structure to a more tractable framework, allowing for a more straightforward mathematical description of the polarization coupling dynamics while still capturing the essential physics governing the conversion process.

Notably, this ring resonator model was found to provide a good fit to the experimentally observed polarization conversion behavior, validating the simplified theoretical approach and confirming that the essential physics of the polarization conversion process can be captured without resorting to more complex full three-dimensional electromagnetic simulations. This agreement between theory and experiment not only strengthens confidence in the underlying physical mechanisms proposed but also establishes a practical and accessible framework for predicting and optimizing polarization conversion performance in similar whispering gallery mode resonator systems for future applications.

# Polarization-Selective Coupling in Whispering Gallery Mode Microresonators

## Introduction and Motivation

Whispering gallery mode (WGM) resonators, particularly silica microspheres, have emerged as versatile platforms for applications ranging from nonlinear optics and cavity quantum electrodynamics to precision sensing and optical frequency comb generation. These resonators support high-quality-factor optical modes that circulate around the equator of a sphere through continuous total internal reflection. While much attention has been devoted to spectral properties, mode volume engineering, and thermal or nonlinear effects in these systems, the polarization behavior of light coupled into and out of WGM resonators remains comparatively underexplored, despite its critical importance for applications requiring precise control over the vectorial nature of light—such as polarization-entangled photon generation, chiral light-matter interactions, and polarization-multiplexed signal processing.

The interaction between a tapered optical fiber and a microsphere resonator is inherently polarization-dependent due to the evanescent coupling mechanism, which is sensitive to the orientation of the electric field relative to the fiber-sphere contact geometry. This dependence opens the possibility of engineering polarization-selective effects, including conversion between orthogonal polarization states, simply by controlling the input polarization and coupling conditions.

## Experimental Setup

In this study, we experimentally investigate polarization-selective phenomena arising from the evanescent coupling between a tapered optical fiber and a silica microsphere whispering gallery mode resonator. The microsphere, fabricated by melting the tip of a standard single-mode optical fiber using a CO2 laser or electric arc discharge, supports high-Q whispering gallery modes accessible through frustrated total internal reflection at the taper waist.

The tapered fiber, pulled to a diameter comparable to the wavelength of the light being used, is brought into the near-field of the microsphere with sub-micron precision using piezoelectric positioning stages. Light from a tunable laser source is launched into the input port of the taper, with a fiber polarization controller placed upstream to allow full control over the input polarization state—spanning the entire Poincaré sphere—before the light reaches the coupling region.

At the output, the transmitted light is analyzed using a combination of a polarization beam splitter and photodetectors, enabling simultaneous monitoring of the two orthogonal polarization components. By systematically varying the input polarization state and the taper-sphere coupling gap, we map out the resonance spectra and polarization-dependent transmission characteristics of the system.

## Polarization Conversion Phenomena

A central finding of this work is the observation of significant polarization conversion at specific resonance conditions. When the input light is prepared in a particular linear polarization state relative to the taper axis, we observe that a substantial fraction of the optical power is coupled into the orthogonal polarization state upon transmission through the coupling region at resonance. This effect arises from the hybrid nature of the whispering gallery modes and the asymmetric coupling geometry between the fiber taper and the spherical resonator, which permits cross-coupling between quasi-TE and quasi-TM-like mode families.

By carefully optimizing the input polarization angle and the taper-sphere gap distance, we systematically characterize the conditions under which this conversion is maximized. Our measurements reveal that the polarization conversion efficiency—defined as the fraction of input power emerging in the orthogonal polarization state at resonance—can reach approximately 75%, representing a highly efficient and reproducible mechanism for polarization manipulation within a compact, all-fiber-coupled system.

## Theoretical Modeling

To gain physical insight into the observed polarization dynamics, we develop a simplified theoretical model based on a two-mode ring resonator framework. In this approach, the whispering gallery resonator is treated as supporting two nearly degenerate polarization eigenmodes that are coupled to each other, either through intrinsic birefringence of the microsphere or through the coupling asymmetry introduced by the tapered fiber itself.

The model incorporates coupled-mode equations describing the evolution of the two polarization components as they propagate through the effective ring cavity, accounting for the input-output coupling rates, intrinsic loss rates, and a cross-coupling term that mediates energy exchange between the two polarization channels. By solving these equations in the steady-state regime and fitting the resulting transmission spectra to the experimental data, we extract the relevant coupling parameters that govern the polarization conversion process.

The excellent agreement between the simplified ring resonator model and the experimental observations confirms that the polarization conversion phenomenon can be understood within a relatively straightforward theoretical framework, without requiring a full vectorial treatment of the microsphere's electromagnetic mode structure. This simplification is particularly valuable for the design and prediction of polarization-selective behavior in future microresonator-based devices.

## Discussion and Implications

The demonstrated ability to achieve approximately 75% polarization conversion efficiency through simple adjustment of input polarization and coupling parameters represents a practical and experimentally accessible method for controlling polarization states in microresonator systems. Unlike approaches that require specialized fabrication techniques, integrated waveplates, or engineered birefringent elements, the method presented here relies solely on the natural coupling physics between a tapered fiber and a spherical resonator, making it readily implementable in standard WGM resonator setups.

This polarization control mechanism has several important implications. First, it suggests that polarization-based multiplexing schemes could be implemented in WGM resonator networks for enhanced information processing capacity. Second, the ability to convert between polarization states at resonance could be exploited in the generation of polarization-entangled photon pairs through nonlinear processes such as spontaneous four-wave mixing, where control over the polarization degrees of freedom of pump, signal, and idler photons is essential. Third, the sensitivity of the polarization conversion efficiency to the taper-sphere gap suggests potential applications in high-precision displacement or refractive index sensing, where polarization state changes could serve as a sensitive readout mechanism.

## Conclusion

This study provides a comprehensive experimental and theoretical investigation of polarization-selective coupling phenomena in a silica microsphere whispering gallery mode resonator coupled to a tapered optical fiber. By optimizing the input polarization state and coupling conditions, we demonstrate efficient polarization conversion of approximately 75%, which is well described by a simplified two-mode ring resonator model incorporating cross-polarization coupling. These results establish a practical and readily accessible approach for polarization state control in microresonator-based photonic systems, with promising implications for applications in quantum photonics, optical signal processing, and precision sensing.

# Experimental Demonstration of Novel Approaches: A Common Thread in Scientific Communication

The phrase "we experimentally demonstrate" appears frequently in scientific literature, particularly in physics, engineering, and materials science papers. This construction serves a crucial rhetorical and scientific function: it signals to readers that the following claims are not merely theoretical predictions or simulations, but results verified through actual laboratory work.

## Why This Phrasing Matters

When researchers write "we experimentally demonstrate," they are making an implicit contrast with purely theoretical or computational work. This distinction is significant in fields where the gap between theory and experimental realization can be substantial. For example:

- **In photonics and optics**: A paper might state "We experimentally demonstrate a novel waveguide design that reduces signal loss by 40%," distinguishing this from prior theoretical proposals.

- **In quantum computing**: Researchers often need to show that quantum phenomena predicted by theory can actually be observed and controlled in physical systems, hence "we experimentally demonstrate quantum entanglement between..."

- **In materials science**: Claims like "we experimentally demonstrate enhanced conductivity in..." validate that laboratory-synthesized materials actually exhibit predicted properties.

## The Structure of Such Claims

Papers using this phrase typically follow a pattern:
1. Background/motivation (what problem exists)
2. Theoretical or conceptual proposal
3. **"We experimentally demonstrate..."** — the pivotal transition to empirical validation
4. Methodology describing the experimental setup
5. Results confirming (or sometimes partially confirming) theoretical predictions

## Broader Significance

This phrasing reflects the scientific method's core requirement: reproducible, empirical verification. In an era where computational modeling and simulation are increasingly sophisticated, explicitly stating that results come from physical experiments (rather than simulations alone) helps readers calibrate their confidence in the findings and understand the maturity of the technology or phenomenon being described.

# Abstract

We report on the phenomenon of polarization conversion between transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) whispering gallery modes (WGMs) in a silica microsphere resonator evanescently coupled to a tapered optical fiber. Whispering gallery mode resonators are known for their ultra-high quality factors and small mode volumes, making them attractive for applications in nonlinear optics, sensing, and cavity quantum electrodynamics; however, polarization-dependent coupling effects can significantly influence device performance and are often overlooked in idealized treatments. In this work, we experimentally and theoretically investigate the coupling dynamics between the tapered fiber and the microsphere, demonstrating that residual ellipticity in the taper waist, microscopic surface inhomogeneities, and the resonator's intrinsic asymmetry induce coherent coupling between nominally orthogonal TE and TM mode families. We observe pronounced polarization conversion signatures in the transmission spectra, manifesting as characteristic avoided-crossing-like features and asymmetric resonance lineshapes when the input polarization state is varied. A coupled-mode theory model incorporating a polarization-coupling coefficient is developed to quantitatively reproduce the observed spectral features, allowing extraction of the effective coupling strength and associated loss channels. Our results reveal that polarization conversion can be systematically controlled through adjustment of the fiber-microsphere gap distance and input polarization angle, providing a pathway toward polarization-selective filtering and mode-conversion devices. These findings have important implications for the design of polarization-maintaining WGM-based photonic devices, as well as for applications requiring precise control of polarization states, such as quantum information processing, optical frequency comb generation, and high-sensitivity biosensing, where uncontrolled polarization mixing can introduce noise or limit device fidelity.

# Efficient Polarization Conversion in Whispering Gallery Mode Resonators: Experimental Optimization and Ring Resonator Modeling

We report on efficient polarization conversion between orthogonally polarized whispering gallery modes (WGMs) in a crystalline microresonator system, achieved through systematic experimental optimization and validated by an analytical ring resonator model. Polarization coupling between transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) mode families is induced via controlled birefringent perturbation, enabling coherent energy transfer at designated spectral positions where phase-matching conditions between the two polarization branches are satisfied. By precisely tuning the coupling geometry and resonator surface conditions, we experimentally demonstrate polarization conversion efficiencies exceeding 90%, accompanied by narrowband spectral signatures indicative of strong mode hybridization near avoided-crossing resonances.

To capture the underlying physics, we develop a simplified ring resonator model incorporating linear mode coupling between two polarization eigenmodes, characterized by a coupling rate, intrinsic and coupling losses, and a detuning parameter representing the polarization-mode splitting. This model reproduces the observed transmission and conversion spectra with high fidelity, allowing extraction of key system parameters including the polarization coupling strength and the critical coupling condition necessary for maximal conversion. We find that the interplay between waveguide-resonator coupling strength and intrinsic polarization mode coupling governs the conversion efficiency, with optimal performance occurring near the critical coupling regime where external losses are matched to the polarization-conversion-induced linewidth broadening.

Our combined experimental and theoretical approach provides clear design guidelines for engineering high-efficiency polarization converters based on WGM resonators, with direct implications for polarization-division multiplexing, quantum photonic interconnects, and integrated polarization-control components in nonlinear and quantum photonic circuits. These results establish the ring resonator framework as a versatile and computationally efficient tool for predicting and optimizing polarization conversion phenomena in high-Q whispering gallery mode systems.
